facts.text: South Yarra was originally inhabited by the Yalukit‑willam clan of the Boonwurrung people who called the area Terneet, the meaning of which has been lost.
The Jam Factory, a former factory converted into an upmarket shopping centre and cinemas, stands as a major landmark in South Yarra.
The Prahran Market, located in South Yarra, is one of Melbourne’s most popular and historic fresh‑produce markets.
South Yarra’s main shopping corridor runs along Toorak Road and Chapel Street, where trendy boutiques, restaurants, nightclubs and café culture thrive.
South Yarra station, on the Pakenham, Cranbourne, Frankston and Sandringham lines, opened in 1874 and helped spur the suburb’s rapid growth.
The Melbourne High School, with its 1930s Gothic main building, is a local landmark and one of the suburb’s heritage‑registered buildings.
